findings.body: javac fails with 'method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types', so the whole services module and any dependent build fail; nothing in this PR can ship.
findings.failure_mode: Compilation error: unresolved method signature at UsernameForm.authenticate.
findings.impact: javac fails with 'method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types', so the whole services module and any dependent build fail; nothing in this PR can ship.
findings.root_cause: The patch added a call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments while only introducing the one-argument overload isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) in the superclass.
findings.suggested_fix: Call the existing overload with the current user, e.g. `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or add a matching no-arg helper in UsernamePasswordForm.
findings.title: UsernameForm calls non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), breaking compilation
findings.trigger: Compiling the services module; the only declaration in the class hierarchy is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) (one argument), and a repository-wide search shows no zero-argument overload anywhere.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 47 in UsernameForm.java calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only declaration in the class hierarchy is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 which requires one argument. The literal search confirms no zero-argument overload exists anywhere in the repository. This will cause a compilation error.

raw_findings.body: The webauthn challenge/conditional-UI attributes are never added to the login form for anonymous users, whereas the deleted code filled them exactly when the user was NOT yet selected. Discoverable-key/conditional passkey login on the initial username/password page stops working, and the patch's own retained assertions (e.g. `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` after oauth.openLoginForm() with no user in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest) will fail.
raw_findings.evidence: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
raw_findings.failure_mode: Behavioral regression: previously working conditional passkey login for not-yet-identified users silently disappears from the login and error forms.
raw_findings.impact: The webauthn challenge/conditional-UI attributes are never added to the login form for anonymous users, whereas the deleted code filled them exactly when the user was NOT yet selected. Discoverable-key/conditional passkey login on the initial username/password page stops working, and the patch's own retained assertions (e.g. `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` after oauth.openLoginForm() with no user in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest) will fail.
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactoring replaced the old `user == null` guard around fillContextForm with a shared helper that inverts it to `user != null`, dropping the previously supported anonymous-login case instead of adding the re-authentication case alongside it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not require a non-null user: return true when passkeys are enabled and either user == null (normal login) or the identified user actually has a passkey credential, e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || user has a passwordless webauthn credential)`.
raw_findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, removing conditional passkey UI from anonymous login
raw_findings.trigger: A realm with passkeys enabled and a user opening the login page normally (no re-authentication, context.getUser() == null); authenticate() and the error challenge() at R137 now gate webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on this helper.

raw_findings.body: The negative assertion 'webauthn button is absent' passes on any driver failure, not only on the intended NoSuchElementException, so a broken page or driver error is silently treated as success and the test loses its ability to detect regressions. The `assertThat(..., nullValue())` is also dead code because findElement never returns null.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test can pass vacuously when the login page fails to render for unrelated reasons, weakening regression coverage of the reauthentication-without-passkeys scenario.
raw_findings.impact: The negative assertion 'webauthn button is absent' passes on any driver failure, not only on the intended NoSuchElementException, so a broken page or driver error is silently treated as success and the test loses its ability to detect regressions. The `assertThat(..., nullValue())` is also dead code because findElement never returns null.
raw_findings.root_cause: Newly added negative assertion uses a hand-rolled try/catch that catches the generic Exception type instead of the specific NoSuchElementException.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the try/catch with `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")))`, as done by the pre-existing tests in this suite.
raw_findings.title: Broad catch(Exception) around negative webauthn-form assertion masks unrelated test failures
raw_findings.trigger: Any exception other than NoSuchElementException thrown inside the try block during reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (e.g. StaleElementReferenceException, WebDriverException, page-load timing issues); the same pattern is duplicated at R312-R317.

raw_findings.body: Without @Override the compiler cannot detect a signature drift; the method would silently stop overriding the base class, re-enabling the authenticator list during conditional-passkey login. All other overrides in this file (fillContextForm, createErrorResponse) carry @Override.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Latent maintainability hazard: accidental de-overriding would compile cleanly and change security-relevant form rendering behavior undetected.
raw_findings.impact: Without @Override the compiler cannot detect a signature drift; the method would silently stop overriding the base class, re-enabling the authenticator list during conditional-passkey login. All other overrides in this file (fillContextForm, createErrorResponse) carry @Override.
raw_findings.root_cause: New override added without the @Override annotation, deviating from the convention used by every other override in the class.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add the @Override annotation to the new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators method.
raw_findings.title: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator lacks @Override annotation
raw_findings.trigger: Any future rename or signature change of WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext) introduced in this same patch.

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that anonymous-login conditional passkey UI is broken is incorrect.
